course_information.title: Loss Prevention Fundamentals
course_information.description: Learn everyday habits that help protect people, merchandise, and store records without confrontation or profiling.
course_information.scope: General; store-specific policies must be supplied separately
course_information.restrictions: No authority to perform inventory adjustments, investigations, detentions, security review, equipment operation, or price overrides without store authorization.
learning_objectives: Explain the difference between loss, shrink, and ordinary inventory error.
Identify everyday practices that reduce preventable loss.
Recognize and report suspicious situations without assumptions or profiling.
Respond safely to theft concerns using store policy.
Protect transaction information and report discrepancies through approved channels.

lessons.title: Understand Loss and Shrink
lessons.objective: Recognize common causes of missing or damaged merchandise.
lessons.why_this_matters: Loss prevention means reducing avoidable losses while keeping employees and customers safe. Shrink is the difference between recorded inventory and the inventory actually accounted for. Theft can contribute, but so can damage, mistakes, miscounts, and process problems.

content_sections.heading: More than theft
content_sections.text: Examples include damaged bags of soil, incorrect receiving quantities, mis-scanned products, and items placed in the wrong location. Never treat a discrepancy alone as proof of theft.

content_sections.heading: People come first
content_sections.text: Safety matters more than merchandise. Follow store policy for incidents and never confront, chase, restrain, or physically intervene with a suspected shoplifter.

lessons.hardware_store_example: A box of screws is counted as twelve cartons instead of twelve pieces. The inventory record is wrong even though no product was stolen.
what_to_say_or_do: Use neutral language such as “inventory difference.”
Report damaged or missing stock using approved channels.
common_mistakes: Trying to recover merchandise by force.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Ask a manager about an unexplained difference or any situation that feels unsafe.

key_takeaways: Use neutral language such as “inventory difference.”

Ask a manager about an unexplained difference or any situation that feels unsafe.

practice.question: A count is short by two items. What can you conclude?

options.text: There is a discrepancy that needs review.
The supplier always shipped too few.

practice.explanation: A shortage alone does not identify a cause.

lessons.title: Reduce Loss Through Daily Habits
lessons.objective: Use routine accuracy and care to reduce preventable loss.
lessons.why_this_matters: Small, consistent actions protect merchandise. Accurate receiving, correct shelf labels, prompt damage reports, and careful transactions all matter.

content_sections.heading: Check products and labels
content_sections.text: Confirm the SKU and unit of measure when receiving or stocking. Keep small or high-value products in approved display locations without inventing new restrictions.

content_sections.heading: Care for merchandise
content_sections.text: Report torn packaging, leaks, and broken displays. Follow the store’s approved damage and disposal process.

content_sections.heading: Keep work areas clear
content_sections.text: A tidy checkout and organized receiving area make mistakes easier to spot. Keep customer walkways safe and maintain visibility according to store policy.

lessons.hardware_store_example: An associate notices two nearly identical drill bits in the same bin. The associate separates them using the correct shelf tags and tells the department lead.
what_to_say_or_do: Ask before moving controlled or secured merchandise.
common_mistakes: Guessing which SKU belongs to a product.
Throwing away damaged stock without recording it.
Moving high-value items without updating approved locations.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Ask the department lead about damaged merchandise, security fixtures, or labeling problems.

supporting_materials.purpose: Only use a verified product or shelf photograph if it improves understanding.
supporting_materials.accessibility: Provide alt text identifying the relevant product/location and instructional point.

key_takeaways: Ask the department lead about damaged merchandise, security fixtures, or labeling problems.

practice.question: Which habit helps prevent avoidable inventory loss?

options.text: Putting similar items in one unlabeled bin.
Recording damage through the approved process.

practice.explanation: Accurate damage records help explain missing or unsellable stock.

lessons.title: Notice Concerns Without Profiling
lessons.objective: Describe objective observations and avoid unfair assumptions.
lessons.why_this_matters: Good loss prevention focuses on behavior and store processes, not on a person’s appearance, age, race, clothing, or other personal traits. Ordinary shopping behavior can have many explanations.

content_sections.heading: Observe facts, not identities
content_sections.text: If a situation raises concern, note what you actually saw and where it happened. Do not label someone a thief or make a claim you cannot support.

content_sections.heading: Use normal customer service
content_sections.text: Offer the same respectful assistance you would offer any customer. Do not follow, intimidate, or accuse a person.

content_sections.heading: Keep reports private
content_sections.text: Share factual concerns only with designated staff using approved channels. Avoid discussing suspicions on the sales floor or in personal group chats.

lessons.hardware_store_example: An employee notices an opened package on a shelf. They report the package location and condition to a manager without accusing nearby shoppers.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Contact a manager when you see damaged packaging, an unsafe situation, or a concerning incident.

practice.question: You find an opened package near several shoppers. What should you report?

options.text: The package condition and exact location.
That a customer definitely stole something.
Nothing, because you did not see the opening.

lessons.title: Respond Safely to Suspected Theft
lessons.objective: Follow safe escalation practices instead of intervening.
lessons.why_this_matters: A loss-prevention concern is never a reason to put yourself or another person in danger. Your role is to stay safe, provide ordinary customer service if appropriate, and alert authorized staff.

content_sections.heading: Do not intervene physically
content_sections.text: Do not chase, block an exit, grab merchandise, search bags, or detain someone. Do not make accusations. Store rules and local laws may place additional limits on staff actions.

content_sections.heading: Get help promptly
content_sections.text: Notify the designated manager or security contact according to store policy. If there is an immediate threat, move to safety and use the store’s emergency procedure.

content_sections.heading: Preserve factual information
content_sections.text: If asked to report an incident, record only what you directly observed, such as time, location, and actions. Do not access or share video unless authorized.

lessons.hardware_store_example: An associate thinks a customer may have left without paying. The associate does not pursue the person. They tell the manager what they directly observed.
common_mistakes: Chasing someone into the parking lot.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Contact a manager immediately for suspected theft; use emergency procedures if anyone is threatened.

practice.question: A customer appears to leave with unpaid merchandise. What is the safest response?

options.text: Notify the designated manager without confrontation.

practice.explanation: Staff safety comes before merchandise recovery.

lessons.title: Protect Transactions and Report Errors
lessons.objective: Use careful checkout and reporting habits.
lessons.why_this_matters: Transaction errors can cause loss even when no one intended harm. Accuracy at checkout, returns, discounts, and cash handling helps the store understand what happened.

content_sections.heading: Verify before completing a transaction
content_sections.text: Use the correct product barcode, quantity, and unit. Follow store procedures for discounts, returns, refunds, and overrides. Never share passwords or use another employee’s credentials.

content_sections.heading: Correct mistakes openly
content_sections.text: If you notice a missed scan, wrong quantity, or incorrect refund, tell an authorized team member and follow the correction process. Do not quietly edit or hide it.

content_sections.heading: Respect privacy
content_sections.text: Keep customer and payment information confidential. Use approved systems and channels for incident reports.

lessons.hardware_store_example: A cashier notices that a customer bought two identical items but only one was scanned. The cashier follows the approved correction process and requests help if the sale is complete.
what_to_say_or_do: Check item quantity and product identifiers.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Ask a supervisor about overrides, cash discrepancies, refunds, or suspected fraud.

options.text: Follow the store’s correction process with authorized help.

practice.explanation: Authorized corrections keep transaction records reliable.
